title: Multi-SDK Atomic Publish Pipeline with Signed Reproducible Artifacts
creator: Priya Patel
description: Unify and harden the publish pipeline for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs into an atomic CI workflow that produces signed, reproducible artifacts and machine-verifiable provenance. Goals: (1) deterministic build outputs (sdist/wheel/npm tarballs/gomod archive), (2) GPG/cosign signing + transparency (rekor), (3) robust registry publishing with retries and OTP/2FA handling, (4) automatic changelog and semantic versioning per-repo, (5) canary/staged publish to test registries, and (6) link SDK release to streaming ergonomics examples and compatibility tests.
acceptance_criteria: A single GitHub Actions workflow or composite pipeline can publish Python/TS/Go artifacts from a tagged commit with one command
All produced artifacts include reproducible metadata (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, deterministic file ordering, pinned build environment) and a checksum file
Artifacts are signed and an attestation/provenance statement is pushed to Sigstore/Rekor and stored in releases
Publish step retries transient failures with exponential backoff and preserves idempotency (no duplicate releases in registries)
Automated changelog is generated from conventional-commit messages and included in the release notes
End-to-end integration test verifies packaging + streaming ergonomics example across supported Python/Node/Go versions
implementation_notes: Versioning decision: use independent semantic versioning per SDK repository; create a composite release tag (e.g., sdk-release/2025-11-05-<hash>) to group a coordinated release
Build reproducibility: set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, normalize file timestamps, use pip wheel --no-build-isolation where possible, docker build with pinned base images and deterministic tar creation

Signing: use Sigstore (cosign) for container/artifact signing + Rekor transparency log; fall back to repo-managed GPG key only for artifacts where cosign is not supported; sign checksums (sha256) for every artifact
- Python: build sdist + wheel, upload via twine with builtin retry wrapper; publish first to TestPyPI canary then PyPI upon health checks
- TypeScript: use npm pack -> verify checksum -> npm publish with otp support; use npm dist-tag (beta -> latest) for staged rollout
- Go: use goreleaser to create archives and push tags; publish to GitHub Packages and ensure GOPROXY publishes metadata; also publish module proxy metadata to proxy.golang.org when available
Provenance: emit in-toto style statement (artifact -> source commit, build env hash, builder image digest) and attach to GitHub Release assets
CI environment: self-hosted runners with access to signing KMS; use short-lived credentials via GitHub OIDC to pull ephemeral signing keys from cloud KMS; no long-lived secret keys stored in repo
Retries and idempotency: use publish tokens with unique upload IDs; if upload partially succeeds, pipeline queries registry for artifact checksum and either completes or reuploads onto mismatch
Canary/staged flow: push to TestPyPI / npm tag beta / GitHub prerelease; run smoke tests (install from registry and run streaming examples) before promoting

Docs and examples: automatically build language-specific streaming ergonomic examples (Python async generator, Node streaming iterator, Go io.Reader) and include them in release notes and examples bundle
Observability: emit metrics for publish latency, retry counts, and signing failures to the Redwood Console (release-engineering dashboard)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Signing keys compromise -> Mitigation: use cloud KMS with OIDC + key rotation; minimize number of keys with signing delegation and audit logs
Risk: Non-deterministic builds -> Mitigation: isolate build steps in pinned container images and create lightweight reproducibility test that compares checksums across builders
Risk: Registry rate limits / transient failures -> Mitigation: exponential backoff with jitter, publish to canaries first, retry idempotently, and surface failures to on-call
Risk: OTP/manual 2FA blocking CI -> Mitigation: use automation-friendly machine accounts with scoped tokens and registry OTP app-OTP fallback path for high-privilege publishes
